description.p: Callie is a calendar for people who live in their calendar. It connects to Google Calendar and any CalDAV server, and gives you day, week, month and agenda views that are quick to read and quick to change.

ul.li: Day, week, month and agenda views
Drag to reschedule, drag to create
Desktop notifications with one-click join for video calls
A companion command-line interface for power users

Outlook and Microsoft 365 accounts: connect one in Settings, under Accounts, or with callie accounts add microsoft. Calendars sync both ways, guests get invitations from Outlook, invitations can be answered, and events can have a Teams link where the account has Teams.
Make and delete calendars on CalDAV servers, under the account in Settings or with callie calendars new <name> --account <id> and callie calendars remove. Deleting asks first.
Save a calendar, or one event, as an .ics file from the calendar's menu in the sidebar or the event's details, or with callie export.
Importing an .ics file into Google keeps a changed occurrence of a repeating event in its series.
The end time list says how long the event would be: it counted a quarter hour short.

description.p: Renaming and recoloring CalDAV calendars on the server, invitations sent by CalDAV servers, .ics files imported into CalDAV and Google calendars, and flat grey disabled buttons.
CalDAV accounts such as Fastmail, iCloud and Nextcloud, calendars kept on this computer, adding events from .ics files, and subscriptions to calendar links.
The week grid fits your working day to the window, base16 color schemes import as themes, and Settings picks where places open from a menu.
Five more built-in themes: Paper, Minimal, Minimal Dark, Tomorrow and Tomorrow Night, with theme menus in Settings and readable invitations in light terminals.
A faster start, a full-screen calendar in the terminal, agenda colors from your theme, upgrade and downgrade commands, a note when a newer release is out, and tab completion for bash, zsh and fish.

Drag an event to the edge of the view to carry it to the next or previous week or month, tooltips with keyboard shortcuts, place settings that stay put, and changes to one occurrence of a repeating event that no longer ask about the whole series.
Installed Callie can connect Google accounts: earlier packages were built without the sign-in client they need.
A system tray entry while Callie keeps running, your working location (Home, Office) under each day's date, overlapping events laid out so every title shows, and a tidier event editor.

Change events as well as create them: edit times, repeats (custom ones too), places with search and maps, guests from your contacts and video calls, move whole series, and undo any change. Changes made offline wait and go once you are back.
Also new: search, an invitations tray, keyboard shortcuts with an optional vi mode, your own calendar names and colors, account photos, the callie command for more tasks, and developer settings.
The first release: a cozy calendar for Linux that keeps up with your Google calendars, with day, week, month and agenda views, quick add, invitations, themes and settings.
